papers.title: Biomimetic Surfaces Coated with Covalently Immobilized Collagen Type I: An X-Ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy, Atomic Force Microscopy, Micro-CT and Histomorphometrical Study in Rabbits.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: The process of osseointegration of dental implants is characterized by healing phenomena at the level of the interface between the surface and the bone. Implant surface modification has been introduced in order to increase the level of osseointegration. The purpose of this study is to evaluate the influence of biofunctional coatings for dental implants and the bone healing response in a rabbit model. The implant surface coated with collagen type I was analyzed through X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS), Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM), micro-CT and histologically. METHODS: The sandblasted and double acid etched surface coated with collagen type I, and uncoated sandblasted and double acid etched surface were evaluated by X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS) and Atomic Force Microscopy (AFM) analysis in order evaluate the different morphology. In vivo, a total of 36 implants were positioned in rabbit articular femoral knee-joint, 18 fixtures for each surface. Micro-CT scans, histological and histomorphometrical analysis were conducted at 15, 30 and 60 days. RESULTS: A histological statistical differences were evident at 15, 30 and 60 days (p < 0.001). Both implant surfaces showed a close interaction with newly formed bone. Mature bone appeared in close contact with the surface of the fixture. The AFM outcome showed a similar roughness for both surfaces. CONCLUSION: However, the final results showed that a coating of collagen type I on the implant surface represents a promising procedure able to improve osseointegration, especially in regions with a low bone quality.

llm.why_not_core: This paper does not involve additive manufacturing (LPBF), porous structure design, stress shielding analysis, or mechanical testing; it focuses solely on surface collagen coating for dental implants.

summary_zh.method: 在喷砂酸蚀表面涂覆I型胶原，通过XPS、AFM、micro-CT和组织学评估。
summary_zh.result: 胶原涂层可改善骨结合，尤其适用于低骨质量区域。
summary_zh.validation: 兔股骨关节植入，15、30、60天组织形态计量学分析。

summary_en.motivation: To enhance osseointegration of dental implants through biofunctional surface coatings.
summary_en.method: Sandblasted and double-acid-etched titanium implants were coated with collagen type I and characterized by XPS, AFM, micro-CT, and histological analysis in a rabbit model.
summary_en.result: Collagen-coated implants showed improved bone-implant contact and mature bone formation compared to uncoated surfaces.
summary_en.validation: In vivo rabbit femoral knee-joint implantation with histomorphometrical evaluation at 15, 30, and 60 days.

papers.title: Adaptive and Safe Bayesian Optimization in High Dimensions via One-Dimensional Subspaces
papers.abstract: Bayesian optimization is known to be difficult to scale to high dimensions, because the acquisition step requires solving a non-convex optimization problem in the same search space. In order to scale the method and keep its benefits, we propose an algorithm (LineBO) that restricts the problem to a sequence of iteratively chosen one-dimensional sub-problems that can be solved efficiently. We show that our algorithm converges globally and obtains a fast local rate when the function is strongly convex. Further, if the objective has an invariant subspace, our method automatically adapts to the effective dimension without changing the algorithm. When combined with the SafeOpt algorithm to solve the sub-problems, we obtain the first safe Bayesian optimization algorithm with theoretical guarantees applicable in high-dimensional settings. We evaluate our method on multiple synthetic benchmarks, where we obtain competitive performance. Further, we deploy our algorithm to optimize the beam intensity of the Swiss Free Electron Laser with up to 40 parameters while satisfying safe operation constraints.

summary_en.motivation: Bayesian optimization struggles in high dimensions due to the non-convex acquisition optimization over the full search space.
summary_en.method: LineBO restricts optimization to a sequence of iteratively chosen one-dimensional subspaces, enabling efficient acquisition.
summary_en.result: The method achieves global convergence, fast local rates under strong convexity, and automatic adaptation to effective dimensionality.
summary_en.validation: Evaluated on synthetic benchmarks and a real-world 40-parameter beam intensity optimization for the Swiss Free Electron Laser.

papers.title: K-nn active learning under local smoothness condition
papers.abstract: There is a large body of work on convergence rates either in passive or active learning. Here we outline some of the results that have been obtained, more specifically in a nonparametric setting under assumptions about the smoothness and the margin noise. We also discuss the relative merits of these underlying assumptions by putting active learning in perspective with recent work on passive learning. We provide a novel active learning algorithm with a rate of convergence better than in passive learning, using a particular smoothness assumption customized for $k$-nearest neighbors. This smoothness assumption provides a dependence on the marginal distribution of the instance space unlike other recent algorithms.   Our algorithm thus avoids the strong density assumption that supposes the existence of the density function of the marginal distribution of the instance space and is therefore more generally applicable.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文研究主动学习算法，与有限元代理模型或生物力学设计无直接关联。
llm.why_not_core: This paper focuses on active learning for classification under smoothness assumptions, with no application to surrogate modeling, expensive simulation sampling, or biomechanical design.

summary_zh.motivation: 在非参数设定下，主动学习收敛率优于被动学习。
summary_zh.method: 提出一种基于局部光滑假设的k近邻主动学习算法。
summary_zh.result: 新算法收敛率优于被动学习，且避免强密度假设。

summary_en.motivation: To achieve better convergence rates in active learning compared to passive learning under nonparametric assumptions.
summary_en.method: A novel active learning algorithm using a local smoothness condition tailored for k-nearest neighbors is proposed.
summary_en.result: The algorithm achieves a superior convergence rate without requiring the existence of a density function for the marginal distribution.
summary_en.validation: Theoretical analysis only, no experimental validation.
